Then we have
$$E = \log_n\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) \log_{n-1}\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) \cdots \log_2\left(\frac{1}{n}\right)$$
$$E = \log_n(2^{-1}) \log_{n-1}(3^{-1}) \cdots \log_2(n^{-1})$$
Using the property $\log_a(x^c) = c \log_a(x)$, we have
$$E = (-1) \log_n(2) (-1) \log_{n-1}(3) \cdots (-1) \log_2(n)$$
Since there are $n-1$ terms in the product, we have $(-1)^{n-1}$ as a factor.
sentence-category-reason: Performs algebraic rewrites using log properties and determines the sign factor by counting terms.

sentence:
Thus
$$E = (-1)^{n-1} \log_n(2) \log_{n-1}(3) \cdots \log_2(n)$$
Using the change of base formula $\log_a(b) = \frac{\log_c(b)}{\log_c(a)}$, we can write
$$E = (-1)^{n-1} \frac{\ln 2}{\ln n} \frac{\ln 3}{\ln (n-1)} \cdots \frac{\ln n}{\ln 2}$$
We can write the terms as
$$E = (-1)^{n-1} \frac{\ln 2}{\ln n} \frac{\ln 3}{\ln (n-1)} \frac{\ln 4}{\ln (n-2)} \cdots \frac{\ln (n-1)}{\ln 3} \frac{\ln n}{\ln 2}$$
We can see that the terms in the numerator and denominator are just rearranged.
sentence-category-reason: Applies the change-of-base formula and rewrites the product into a cancellable form, executing computational steps.

sentence: Therefore, we can cancel terms from the end to the beginning.

sentence:
$$E = (-1)^{n-1} \frac{\ln 2 \ln 3 \cdots \ln n}{\ln n \ln (n-1) \cdots \ln 2}$$
$$E = (-1)^{n-1} \frac{\ln 2}{\ln 2} \frac{\ln 3}{\ln 3} \cdots \frac{\ln n}{\ln n}$$
Therefore,
$$E = (-1)^{n-1} \cdot 1 = (-1)^{n-1}$$
Thus, the expression simplifies to $(-1)^{n-1}$.
